about: Written on 2026-10-23 by a Claude agent asked only to label data, before any AI-answer sentiment classifier existed and without reading any classifier code: the 70 hold-out cases (H) were written from scratch, with invented business names for every criticism, and the 40 real cases (R) are sentences from AI answers stored in harness/fixtures_live, kept verbatim or lightly trimmed. Polarity is about the named business only: a stated official accreditation, approval or certification counts as trust positive, a plain list item or description is neutral, and a mixed statement takes the side a buyer would take away (usually the clause after 'but'). An aspect with polarity 'neutral' marks a dimension the text describes without judging; the stored real answers contain no criticism of a named business, so the negative class is covered by the hold-out only. The tuning cases (T) were written afterwards by W2-E2 to build the rule reader; the rules were built on them only, and the hold-out and real cases were scored once, at the end. Round 1 (2026-10-23): the rules built on the T cases scored polarity kappa 0.587 on the 70 H cases and 0.697 on the 40 R cases, read once; the H and R cases were then used to improve the rules (split "holdout1"), and a second blind hold-out (K cases) was written by another labelling agent and scored once, at the end. Hold-out round 2 (K cases): Blind hold-out for the aspect-based sentiment of AI-assistant answers about a business, written by a labelling agent on 2026-10-23 before scoring. The classifier's author has never seen these cases; every business name is invented. Polarity is judged for the named business only; mixed statements take the side a buyer would take away. Round 2 result (scored once, 2026-10-23): the rule reader reached polarity kappa 0.548 on the 80 blind K cases (accuracy 70%), below the 0.7 bar, so the rules are NOT used for any published figure: only the model (Claude Haiku) labels count, and the rules are a second opinion whose agreement is printed.
